newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA AND REAL BETIS TACTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA AND REAL BETIS TACTICS.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Barcelona and Real Betis who contest the Spanish Cup final at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium on Saturday (kick-off 1900 GMT):
Barcelona:

Strategy: Manager Bobby Robson has used a number of tactical formations during the course of the season but is expected to adopt the 4-2-3-1 strategy which bought him success in the European Cup Winners' Cup final last month.

The former England coach has been criticised by the Spanish media and Barcelona fans for producing a side which plays dull football, relying on getting the ball to a front man with as little fuss as possible.
Nevertheless he has achieved excellent results, reaching two Cup finals and finishing a close second to Real Madrid in the Spanish first division.
Josep Guardiola and Gheorghe Popescu are the main playmakers. Luis Figo and Luis Enrique are exceptionally active on the flanks and Ivan de la Pena acts as main provider for the front man.

Juan Pizzi looks set to be given the goalscoring responsibility in the likely absence of Brazil's Ronaldo, who is playing in the Copa America. But Robson may still opt for the experience of Bulgarian Hristo Stoichkov, with expectations running so high.

Strengths: Central defenders Abdelardo and Fernando Couto are one of the best pairings in European soccer, very solid. Opposing teams often decide to go wide rather than through the middle due to the expertise of the Barcelona pair.
Guardiola is among the most skilful players in Spain and can distribute the ball with pinpoint accuracy.
Sergi and Luis Enrique are tireless workers down the left wing and overlap to give opposing defences immense problems because of their speed and stamina.
De la Pena on his day is one of the most exciting players in Europe with his dribbling skills and has an outstanding ability to get the ball to the strikers.
Robson's side have also been outstanding at set-pieces, with many of their goals generated from dead-ball situations.
Weaknesses: Goalkeeper Vitor Baia has lost some of the form which made him one of the world's best in 1996. In recent months he has become prone to previously uncharacteristic errors.
Albert Ferrer is the weak link in the defence and opponents often attack down his flank to exploit his lack of physical presence. Back-up defender Laurent Blanc also struggles out on the right.

The likely absence of Ronaldo, at the Copa America and caught up in transfer wrangling, means Robson may have to rely on Pizzi, who been second choice all season and struggled to get many games. Pizzi has also gained a reputation for squandering good goal chances.
Robson has the players who can get the ball into scoring positions but, without Ronaldo, lacks a first-rate finisher.
Midfield men, particularly de la Pena, have a habit of pushing forward in frustration and leaving gaps behind them if the game is close.
Motivation: Robson wants to keep his job at Barcelona after season-long speculation that he will be given the sack if he does not succeed -- and the players, with a few exceptions, like Robson.
Likely team: Vitor Baia, Albert Ferrer, Abdelardo Fernadez, Fernando Couto, Sergi Barjuan, Josep Guardiola, Gheorghe Popescu, Ivan de la Pena, Luis Enrique, Luis Figo, Juan Pizzi.
Real Betis

Strategy: Coach Lorenzo Serra Ferrer usually employs a flat back four but varies the midfield formation. He often adopts a standard 4-4-2 strategy but against stronger, attacking teams has used five men in midfield and left Alfonso to toil alone up front. He may well choose this tactic on Saturday.
He has favoured Juan Merino at left back in recent weeks but may opt for the speedy Luis Fernandez to counter the threat of Luis Figo.
Alexis Trujillo and Tomas Olias are likely to drop back deeper than normal to help out the defence, with Juan Canas providing the service in central midfield.
Robert Jarni and Finidi George are expected to work down the wings.
If Sanz does decide to deploy a 4-4-2 formation then Pier Cherubino could accompany Alfonso at the expense of Canas.
Strengths: Serra Ferrer is an outstanding coach, nicknamed El Brujo - the wizard - in Seville. He has turned round the fortunes of a once-mediocre club and given the players new confidence.
Alfonso is a deadly marksman and finished second in the Spanish league scoring standings behind Ronaldo.
Defender Roberto Rios has improved to such an extent that he is now a regular in the Spanish national team.
Down the flanks Jarni and George have terrorised defences all season. Jarni is arguably the star of the team with his excellent crosses into the box and outstanding free kicks.
Trujillo is an inspirational captain as well as a skilled midfielder.

Weaknesses: Club harmony was shattered by the announcement last week that Serra Ferrer was leaving the club to join Barcelona after the final. He was immediately sacked and then reinstated by club owner Manuel Ruiz de Lopera but the final will be his last game for the club.

There is also a dilemma over who will be the goalkeeper. Toni Prats has been first choice for most of the season but his form has dipped recently. Pedro Jaro, the Spanish league's top goalkeeper in the 1994-95 season, was brought in for the last league match against Valladolid and recaptured his old form. The Spanish media are speculating that Jaro could be a surprise choice on Saturday.
Betis's defence is also far from secure, apart from Rios. The right side is particularly vulnerable despite the presence of Yugoslav internationals Hristo Vidakovic and Albert Nadj.

George's match fitness is also open to question. The Nigerian returned to action only recently after knee-ligament operations. There are serious doubts over whether he will last 90 minutes against a team like Barcelona, so Serra Ferrer must decide whether to include him in the starting line-up or save him for later.

Motivation: To give Serra Ferrer a winning send-off and also defy the odds which make Barcelona prohibitive favourites. However, Betis know their place in next season's Cup Winners' Cup is secure as Barcelona will be Spain's second representatives in the European Cup.
Likely team: Pedro Jaro, Albert Nadj, Hristo Vidakovic, Roberto Rios, Juan Merino, Alexis Trujillo, Juan Canas, Tomas Olias, Robert Jarni, Finidi George, Alfonso Perez.
